phrase: If you’re not paying for the product, you are the product
aliases: if you are not paying for it you are the product
youre not the customer youre the product
finding: Popular 2010 MetaFilter wording is distinct from a 1973 video-art antecedent; popularization and origin are separate, and the TV critique is related rather than identical wording.
searchScope: Quote Investigator dossier, MetaFilter 2010 comment trail via QI, and Richard Serra / Carlota Fay Schoolman 1973 video documentation.
evidenceReviewed: QI (2017) on Television Delivers People (1973) and Andrew Lewis / blue_beetle MetaFilter (2010); MoMA/video documentation summaries.

assertions.subject: Television Delivers People (1973)
assertions.publicStatement: An earlier related formulation appears in Richard Serra and Carlota Fay Schoolman’s 1973 video Television Delivers People: “You are the product of t.v.” — related idea, not the later “if you’re not paying…” wording.

assertions.subject: MetaFilter comment by Andrew Lewis (2010)
assertions.publicStatement: Earliest verified occurrence located for the modern “if you are not paying…” formulation: Andrew Lewis (blue_beetle) on MetaFilter in 2010.
assertions.caveat: Earlier near-matches (for example 2001 Usenet “You’re not the customer, you’re the product”) exist without the payment clause; this page separates those roles.

assertions.subject: Social-media / surveillance-capitalism critique (2010s)
assertions.publicStatement: Popularized by 2010s social-media criticism that recycled the MetaFilter line as a critique of free consumer platforms.

assertions.subject: Andrew Lewis (blue_beetle) for the payment-clause form
assertions.publicStatement: Commonly credited to Andrew Lewis’s 2010 MetaFilter comment for the payment-clause form; that credit covers the modern wording, not the 1973 antecedent.

sources.title: Television Delivers People
sources.author: Richard Serra; Carlota Fay Schoolman
sources.shortExcerpt: You are the product of t.v. You are delivered to the advertiser who is the customer.

sources.title: MetaFilter comment on Digg / user-as-product
sources.author: Andrew Lewis (blue_beetle)
sources.shortExcerpt: If you are not paying for it, you’re not the customer; you’re the product being sold.

sources.title: You’re Not the Customer; You’re the Product
sources.author: Garson O’Toole
sources.shortExcerpt: In conclusion, this saying evolved over time. Richard Serra and Carlota Fay Schoolman crafted an interesting precursor in 1973.
